item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q005_cupredoxin_function_transfer","answer":"In SCOPe 2.08, all three are all-beta domains in the Cupredoxin-like fold b.6 (SUNID 49502) and, more specifically, the Cupredoxins superfamily b.6.1 (SUNID 49503). Thus SCOPe supports probable remote common ancestry, not merely a similar fold. They remain separate families: Plastocyanin/azurin-like b.6.1.1 (SUNID 49504), Ephrin ectodomain b.6.1.5 (SUNID 74874), and the PAD4 N-terminal domain b.6.1.6 (SUNID 110107). Family separation and their divergent biological roles preclude automatic function transfer. Copper binding and electron transfer must not be inferred for ephrin ectodomains or PAD4 from a plastocyanin/azurin template—and should not be assumed universally even within a structural grouping. Such assignments require target-specific evidence, including conservation and compatible geometry of copper-ligating residues, observed metal/cofactor occupancy, and biochemical, spectroscopic, or redox/electron-transfer measurements. A cupredoxin representative may be used cautiously as a structural template for the corresponding domain scaffold, but not as a functional template or as evidence about full-length multidomain PAD4; representative choice does not override family identity, domain boundaries, or missing active-site evidence.","evidence_used":["mcp__scope__get_scop_service_info: /api/v1/; /api/v1/releases/current","mcp__scope__search_scop: /api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=ephrin&mode=auto&limit=20; /api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=plastocyanin&mode=auto&limit=20; /api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=azurin&mode=auto&limit=20; /api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=Pad4&mode=auto&limit=20","mcp__scope__get_scop_node: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/b.6; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/b.6/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/b.6.1; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/b.6.1/parents","mcp__scope__list_scop_children: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/49503/children?limit=100"]}]}
